rationale: A is much more decision-useful because it compares multiple live alternatives, gives a concrete recommendation with conditional switches, and identifies when load time should override the default choice. Its quantitative estimates and confidence intervals meaningfully help discriminate among options. B is clear and concise, but it under-analyzes key alternatives—especially distribution partnerships—and gives little uncertainty handling or numerical grounding. B’s recommendation could be right in some cases, but it offers less help to a careful decision-maker trying to choose under real constraints.
